description.value: This double-blinded, random-order cross-over study examined the effects of fructose versus glucose ingestion on brain, hormone, appetitive, and food-approach responses in healthy volunteers.

spans.text: Twenty-four healthy volunteers underwent two functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) sessions with ingestion of either fructose or glucose in a double-blinded, random-order cross-over design.

value: We hypothesized that ingestion of fructose compared with glucose would result in greater food-cue reactivity in brain reward regions, greater appetitive responses to food cues, and increased decisions for immediate food rewards over delayed monetary rewards.

description.value: After an overnight fast, participants ingested a fructose, glucose, or water drink and entered the MRI scanner. They viewed randomized blocks of high-calorie food photographs and neutral nonfood photographs. After each block, they rated hunger and desire for food using visual analog scales. Twelve blocks were presented, each containing four photographs shown in random order.

spans.text: They then ingested the study drink (i.e., fructose, glucose, or water) before entering the MRI scanner, where they performed a food-cue task in which 12 visual activation task blocks including food cues and nonfood cues were presented in a randomized block design.
